sentences.text: Researchers investigated how the SARS-CoV-2 virus triggers sneezing, coughing, and pain by using mice and human cells grown from stem cells to test if a specific virus enzyme directly activates airway pain nerves.

When the virus enzyme acted on the nerves, it caused sneezing, coughing, pain, and the release of a specific chemical signal, a process that required both the enzyme and a specific nerve channel while also changing the genes the nerves expressed to turn up the pathway linking the enzyme to the pain channel.
Other coronaviruses that infect mice also caused sneezing in the animal subjects, and this sneezing similarly required the same specific nerve channel.
The authors concluded that the virus enzyme and a specific nerve channel are necessary for the sneeze reflex to happen, noting that these findings were observed in mice and human cells.
